title: Optimizing Data Acquisitions in Multi-Robot Systems
problem: Multi-robot systems lack efficient mechanisms for real-time cross-robot data acquisition; traditional file systems fail to exploit robot data temporal locality
motivation: Multi-robot coordination requires timely data sharing; improving data freshness and query latency enables collaborative robotics at scale
method: ROSfs is a user-level filesystem (a software layer that runs above the operating system) that organizes sensor data from multiple robots by timestamp. Instead of searching through nested folders, one robot can query another robot's data by time—for example, 'send me all camera images from the last 30 seconds'—and get instant access. The system works with ROS (Robot Operating System), the standard software used in robotics, and was tested on real UAV (drone) and UGV (ground robot) systems to confirm it handles real-world scenarios.
key_novelty: The core idea is time-indexed queries—organizing data by timestamp so robot teams can instantly access each other's recent information instead of searching through files.
contributions: Novel labeled sub-file data organization for robot data
7x reduction in online data query latency
271x improvement in data freshness (Age of Information)
limitations: Limited to ROS platform; wireless network evaluation only; scalability to large robot swarms not demonstrated
